decisions.label: Byte order
evidence: The binary header only makes sense read this way.

decisions.label: Samples per trace
evidence: File size divides exactly into traces of this length.

decisions.label: Sample format
evidence: Samples decoded as format 3 (2-byte two's complement integer) look like seismic data (plausibility 1.00, best of all candidates).

decisions.label: Data type
evidence: Bytes 189-192 and 193-196 together give a unique grid position for 100.0% of 414 sampled traces; the first stays constant for runs of traces while the second steps by 1.
The inline number is also stored in byte(s) 9, 11, 191; byte 189 was chosen as the conventional location.
The crossline number is also stored in byte(s) 17, 19, 21, 23, 195; byte 193 was chosen as the conventional location.
Coordinates in bytes 181 and 185 are an exact linear function of (inline, crossline): residual 0.12% of a bin, a perfect regular grid.
The textual header (line 6) gives the inline range 111-133, matching the data.
The textual header (line 7) gives the crossline range 875-892, matching the data.

issues.title: Trace headers carry a different sample count
issues.detail: The first trace header (bytes 115-116) says 462 samples, but the file layout proves 75. This is typical of files that were cropped in time without updating the trace headers.
issues.fix: The fixed file writes 75 into every trace header.
issues.explain: Some loaders read the per-trace sample count instead of the file-level one and will mis-read this file.

actions: Added a provenance stamp to blank lines of the textual header (original text kept).
